<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />{{GHGmargin-letter|113|gg}}
Rem. The subject is sometimes added to the infinitive absolute when it takes the place of the finite verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=6|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=1}}. So, probably, also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=48}}, although here {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־זָכָר}} according to {{GHGpar|121|a}} might also be taken as ''an object'' with a passive verb; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=13}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=26}}, 33 the subject follows an infinitive absolute which is co-ordinated with an infinitive construct, see above, ''e''.<section end=par113 />

<section begin=par114 />{{GHGpar-heading|114|The Infinitive Construct}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|a}}
'''1.''' The infinitive construct, like the infinitive absolute, may also represent a ''nomen verbale'' ({{GHGpar|45|a}}), but of a much more flexible character than the infinitive absolute (cf. {{GHGpar|113|a}}). Its close relation with nouns properly so called is especially seen in the readiness with which the infinitive construct may be used for any case whatever; thus,

(''a'') As the nominative of the subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָֽאָדָם לְבַדּוֹ}}, literally, ''not good is the being of man in his separation''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, 24 (but cf. 21:9 {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב לָשֶׁ֫בֶת}} in the same statement); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=9}} prop. ''there is not a coming near unto thee'', but the text is probably corrupt. With a ''feminine'' predicate, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|b}}
(''b'') As genitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=עֵת סְפוֹד וְעֵת רְקוֹד|translate=a time of mourning and a time of dancing}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=12|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=14}}. This equally includes, according to {{GHGpar|101|a}}, all those cases in which the infinitive construct depends on a preposition (see below, ''d'') [and Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 206].

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|c}}
(''c'') As accusative of the object, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אֵדַע צֵאת וָבֹא|translate=I know not the going out or the coming in}} (''I know not'' how ''to go out and come in''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=28|hidebook=1}} (even with {{GHGheb|text=אֵת}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=22}} (cf. for the use of the infinitive absolute as object, {{GHGpar|113|f}}); as accusative with a verb expressing fullness, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=11|verse=9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|d}}
'''2.''' The construction of the infinitive with prepositions (as in Greek, ἐν τῷ εἶναι, διὰ τὸ εἶναι, &c.) may usually be resolved in English into the finite verb with a conjunction, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּפִגְעוֹ־בוֹ|translate=in his meeting him}}, i.e. if (as soon as) he meets him; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=45}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַד־שׁוּב}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן מָֽאָסְכֶם|translate=because ye despise}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=35}} {{GHGheb|text=עַל־אָמְרֵךְ|translate=because thou sayest}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=1}} ''and his eyes were dim'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵרְאֹת|translate=from seeing}}, i.e. so that he could not see.

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|e}}
This use of the infinitive construct is especially frequent in connexion with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} to express time-determinations (in English resolved into a temporal clause, as above the combination of the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫עַן}} or {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}} is resolved into a causal clause), especially after {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} (see the<section end=par114 /><noinclude>
